newsitem.title: LEBANON: BLC stars on Beirut Stock Exchange.
newsitem.headline: BLC stars on Beirut Stock Exchange.

text.p: Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce (BLC), the first bank listed on the Beirut Stock Exchange since it reopened last January, gave a star performance on its first week of trading.
Shares in BLC closed at $11.75 on Friday on turnover of 10,000 shares compared with $11.50 on Thursday. BLC shares began trading on Monday at $11.25 when 2,000 changed hands.

Solidere also rose on increased turnover on Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ended on Friday. A shares rose 2.05 percent to $112 from $109.75 last Friday and B shares rose 0.88 percent to $115 from $114.
There was no trade on the exchange, which now lists shares of six companies, on Tuesday or Wednesday due to the New Year holiday.
"This is a new instrument on the market and there's always high demand for a new instrument," one dealer said, commenting on the performance of the BLC shares.

"BLC was the first bank to list on the exchange and it did so on the heels of good news; after a capital increase and an issue of GDRs. We hear there is demand for the GDRs abroad like there is demand now for the shares here," the dealer added.

In December, BLC completed a $60-million capital increase through the first simultaneous local and international share offering by a Lebanese issuer. Two-thirds were in Global Depositary Receipts and one-third in a local share offering.

BLC offered 1,227,240 C shares on the Beirut market, and more than three million B shares underlying the GDRs will also be listed later -- which effectively will add some $50 million to the market's current capitalisation of some $2.5 billion.
